criteria_snapshot.name: Technical Capability
criteria_snapshot.description: Fit of the proposed enterprise AI platform: architecture, RAG and enterprise search design, integrations with existing systems, scalability and model choices.

criteria_snapshot.name: Implementation Plan
criteria_snapshot.description: Credibility of delivery: phased timeline, milestones, team structure and staffing, dependencies, and how delivery risks will be managed.

criteria_snapshot.name: Commercial Value
criteria_snapshot.description: Pricing clarity and total cost of ownership: licence and services costs, stated assumptions, exclusions, and value relative to scope.

criteria_snapshot.name: Security & Compliance
criteria_snapshot.description: Security controls, data privacy and residency, access control, audit logging, AI governance, and claimed certifications.

criteria_snapshot.name: Support & Experience
criteria_snapshot.description: Post-go-live support model and SLAs, comparable enterprise AI projects, and customer references.

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: The proposal describes a specific architecture with hybrid retrieval, reranking, citations, a multi-provider model gateway, named connectors, permission-aware retrieval, and stated load-test and evaluation targets. Specific model providers or model choices are not identified, and the performance figures are vendor claims.
evidence: Hybrid retrieval: vector search combined with keyword (BM25) search and a cross-encoder re-ranker.
Prebuilt connectors for SharePoint Online, Confluence Cloud, ServiceNow and SAP S/4HANA (OData).
Load-tested by Apex to 20 million documents and 5,000 concurrent users.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: A 24-week, three-phase plan includes phase durations, outcomes, a 300-user pilot, an 11-person team, and a stated client dependency. The proposal identifies some risks and mitigations, but does not provide detailed milestone acceptance criteria, named staffing commitments, or a broader delivery-risk process.
evidence: We propose a 24-week, three-phase delivery with a 300-user pilot before enterprise rollout.

An 11-person team: engagement lead, project manager, solution architect, security architect, two ML engineers, three data and integration engineers, a QA engineer and a part-time change management lead.
Any delay moves the plan day for day.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: The proposal itemizes annual subscription, fixed implementation services, optional premium support, a three-year total, and estimated Azure consumption. Azure costs are variable and billed separately; content cleansing is excluded, and details such as renewal pricing and the assumptions behind the cloud estimate are not given.
evidence:
Platform subscription (up to 5,000 users), per year
420,000

Three-year total (subscription + implementation)
1,645,000
Azure consumption is billed to Northwind directly (estimated USD 8,000-12,000 per month).

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: The proposal states specific encryption, key-management, residency, training-data, access-control, logging, PII-redaction, and red-team measures. Certification and control statements are vendor claims, and the proposal identifies the certificates and report as fictional for this exercise; their validity cannot be established from the proposal.
evidence: AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, customer-managed keys supported.
Data residency in the Azure region selected by Northwind; no customer data is used to train models.
Role-based access control; prompts and responses are audit-logged to Northwind's SIEM for 12 months.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: The proposal gives response targets for P1 and P2 incidents, describes standard and optional premium support, and states that quarterly model performance reviews are included. The cited references are explicitly fictional, so they do not substantiate comparable project experience; resolution targets and other support service details are also not stated.
evidence: Standard support is business hours (9x5).
P1 incidents are handled 24x7 with a one-hour response target; P2 incidents within four business hours.
Both references are fictional for this exercise.

risks: The proposal identifies itself as a synthetic proposal for an academic exercise; its supplier, capability, delivery, pricing, security, and experience statements are not verified facts.
The proposal explicitly says the ISO certificate and SOC 2 report are fictional, and that both customer references are fictional; they do not substantiate real-world compliance or experience.
Azure consumption is an additional variable cost billed directly to Northwind, and the proposal gives only an estimate.
Legacy content cleansing is excluded and may require separately quoted work.
The schedule depends on Northwind providing an Azure subscription and connector service accounts by week 3; delays shift the plan day for day.
The stated 24x7 support for all priorities is optional and carries a separate annual charge.
missing_information: Specific model names or providers, selection rationale, and model-specific performance or fallback details.
Evidence substantiating the stated scalability, evaluation targets, and integration capabilities.
Detailed implementation milestone acceptance criteria, staffing allocation over time, and delivery governance.
Azure consumption estimate assumptions, subscription renewal terms, and other potential recurring or variable costs.
Verifiable compliance artifacts and details of audit scope, controls, and remediation status.
Support resolution targets, escalation process, service availability commitments, and support coverage details beyond the stated response targets.
Verifiable customer references or other evidence of comparable enterprise AI deployments.
suppliers.overall_summary: The proposal is specific across architecture, integrations, implementation phases, pricing, and stated security controls. Its principal limitations are that all content is explicitly fictional for an academic exercise, including the cited certifications and references, and that several claims cannot be verified from the proposal. Variable Azure costs, excluded content cleansing, client-side dependencies, and limited support-detail commitments also warrant clarification.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: The proposal specifies round-the-clock support, response and resolution targets, an uptime SLA, service credits, hypercare, and named customer-success coverage. It claims 16 deployments and names two references, but explicitly says those references are fictional, so comparable experience is not substantiated.

risks: The proposal identifies itself as synthetic, and explicitly states that the named references are fictional; claimed experience and customer outcomes are therefore not verifiable from this proposal.
The ISO/IEC 27001 certificate is explicitly described as fictional, and SOC 2 Type II is still in progress.
The stated test scale is up to 2 million documents, while the commercial assumption covers 5 million documents; capacity and performance at the assumed scale are not evidenced.
Northwind-tenant cloud hosting costs are billed separately to Northwind and are not quantified in the stated three-year total.
The SOC 2 Type II audit is expected Q2 2027, so its completion is not established by the proposal.
missing_information: Specific model options, model-selection rationale, and associated performance or cost assumptions.
Evidence or detailed capacity and performance targets for operation at the assumed five-million-document scale.
Quantified Northwind cloud-hosting costs and a fuller list of commercial exclusions and assumptions.
Verifiable certification documentation and supporting security/compliance evidence, including the status and scope of audits.
Detailed AI-governance processes, privacy controls, and audit-log access and review procedures.
Verifiable customer references or evidence supporting the claimed 16 deployments.
Phase-by-phase staffing allocation and contingency plans for schedule or dependency delays.
suppliers.overall_summary: NexaWorks presents a structured proposal with a concrete architecture outline, phased implementation plan, defined team, and specific support targets. Pricing is comparatively clear but excludes unquantified customer-tenant hosting costs. Security and experience claims require substantial validation because the proposal labels its certificate and references fictional and describes SOC 2 Type II as still in progress.

suppliers.overall_summary: BrightPath Tech provides a concise proposal with a basic SaaS architecture, a stated eight-week implementation schedule, itemized headline pricing, and limited support and security commitments. Important details are absent across technical design, delivery dependencies, commercial assumptions, security and governance, and customer evidence. The stated ISO 27001 certification is not yet achieved according to the proposal.

tie_break_rules: Higher Peer Performance Index (PPI) ranks first.
If PPI is equal: earlier submission date ranks first.
If still equal: higher historical experience rating ranks first.
If still equal: supplier name in alphabetical order (A to Z).

formulas.benchmark: highest assessed score per criterion among non-FAILED suppliers
formulas.ppi: sum(weight * relative_pct) / sum(weight); rounded half-up to 2 dp; ranking uses rounded PPI

note: Synthetic proposals; supplier statements are unverified vendor claims.
